newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close flat in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close flat in listless trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed flat in listless trade on Monday with prices confined to tight ranges amid a lack of significant economic data or news, dealers said.

"I wouldn't say that there's anything memorable about this day," said Hank Cunningham, a bond trader with First Marathon Securities. "The yield curve steepened a bit more. There's a squeeze on in the two-year bond."
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 traded unchanged at C$102.50 to yield 7.775 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 4/32 to yield 6.94 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 84 basis points from 83 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

"It's really been in a very, very tight range, tighter than we've seen in a lot of recent days. I can't say there was a lot of activity and the dollar was stable. There's no news to move the market one way or the other," said one Toronto-based portfolio manager.

Analysts said the market is awaiting economic data which will provide a better indication of what the U.S. Federal Reserve's next move will be. Key data expected tomorrow includes the U.S. industrial production report.
Statistics Canada will release manufacturing and wage settlements data for July on Tuesday.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.01 to C$98.05 to yield 7.272 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 1/32 to yield 6.72 percent.
The spread between the two bonds widened to 55 basis points from 54 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.73 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.18 percent.
